implementer_questions_answered.question: Does useModalDismiss correctly handle unmount cleanup? If the modal unmounts before onClose fires, does the body overflow get restored?
implementer_questions_answered.answer: YES · verified. Lines 73-81 · useEffect cleanup fires on both open→false transitions AND on component unmount (React's guarantee). `prev` is captured at open-time via closure and the cleanup returns overflow to that captured value. Unmount scenario: cleanup restores overflow=prev · no orphan lock. Verified by re-reading the effect. No fix needed.

implementer_questions_answered.question: Focus trap: if the container has NO focusable children, does the hook no-op cleanly?
implementer_questions_answered.answer: YES · line 94 `if (focusable.length === 0) return;` short-circuits the Tab handler. e.preventDefault is never called, first/last are never referenced. Message-only modals are safe. No fix needed.

implementer_questions_answered.question: Multiple concurrent modals — do the two Esc handlers stack correctly (capture-phase stopPropagation would only reach the top-most, right)?
implementer_questions_answered.answer: NO · this is a real bug. See P1-003. The hook's docblock at line 58 claims 'capture-phase so a nested modal above a drawer gets it first' but the implementation at line 67 registers with default (bubble) phase — no `{ capture: true }`. Furthermore, even in capture phase, `e.stopPropagation()` does NOT stop sibling listeners on the SAME event target (window). Only stopImmediatePropagation would. Both modals' handlers fire → both close simultaneously.

implementer_questions_answered.question: Body scroll lock stacking — if two modals open in sequence, does the second's cleanup restore the first's `hidden` state?
implementer_questions_answered.answer: PARTIAL · works for LIFO close order (top-most closes first), breaks for arbitrary close order. See P2-009. Modal A opens (captures prev_A=''), Modal B opens on top (captures prev_B='hidden'). If B closes first: restores 'hidden' (correct, A holds lock). If A closes first while B still open: A's cleanup restores overflow='' (wrong · body scrolls while B still visible). Edge case, but real.

findings.summary: Docblock claims capture-phase Esc handler, but implementation uses default bubble phase without `{ capture: true }`. This defeats the stated design intent AND allows concurrent modals to close simultaneously on a single Esc keystroke because stopPropagation does not block sibling listeners on the same target (window).
findings.evidence: Line 58 comment: 'Esc — capture-phase so a nested modal above a drawer gets it first.' Line 67: `window.addEventListener("keydown", handler);` — no options object, so useCapture=false (bubble phase). Furthermore, when PublishModal is open and WatermarkTrialConfirmModal opens on top (real scenario: ExportPanel opens WatermarkTrialConfirmModal while PublishModal is separately open in EditorSection), both modals register handlers on `window`. Esc fires both listeners in registration order. `e.stopPropagation()` blocks propagation to OTHER nodes but NOT to sibling listeners on the same target — only `e.stopImmediatePropagation()` blocks siblings. Result: hitting Esc closes BOTH modals in one keystroke.
findings.reproduce: grep -n 'capture-phase\|window.addEventListener' desktop-2/src/lib/useModalDismiss.ts && node -e 'const w = new (require("events").EventEmitter)(); w.on("esc", () => console.log("A")); w.on("esc", (e) => { console.log("B"); }); w.emit("esc");' # illustrates that stopPropagation-in-A does not block B in DOM semantics
findings.suggested_fix: Either (a) integrate with existing `useRegisterModal` in ModalPortal.tsx which already implements LIFO stack semantics + only top modal handles Esc (see P1-005), OR (b) add `{ capture: true }` on the listener AND swap `e.stopPropagation()` for `e.stopImmediatePropagation()` in the handler. Fix in one place — do not ship two competing Esc systems.

findings.summary: The 'silent-error swallow fix' is DEAD CODE. startAssistedHandoff cannot throw and does not emit error toasts on any failure path, so the for-loop's try/catch and the `if (successes > 0)` guard are unreachable. The comment claiming 'per-record failure toasts still fire from startAssistedHandoff' is factually wrong.
findings.evidence: assistedSchedule.ts:211-244 · startAssistedHandoff · every error path is caught internally (writeText@215, revealItemInDir@228, both fall through) or is synchronous+unable-to-throw (openWith unawaited @235, patchAssistedJob @236, bus.emit @237). Only one bus.emit exists — kind:'success' at line 237. There is no `bus.emit({kind:'error', ...})` anywhere in the file. So `await startAssistedHandoff(record)` never rejects, the `catch` at PublishModal:246 never runs, `successes` always equals `channels.length`, and the `if (successes > 0)` guard is trivially true. The Batch 1 goal of 'no silent success lie' is not achieved.
findings.suggested_fix: Two-part fix: (a) inside startAssistedHandoff, catch openWith failure explicitly and emit an error toast when the browser overlay fails to open; propagate the throw so callers can count it; (b) the caption/reveal 'best-effort' swallows are OK but at least log a warning via a diagnostics channel. Once (a) lands, PublishModal's success-counting branch becomes real and meaningful. Until then, delete the dead try/catch to avoid documenting a fix that doesn't function.

findings.summary: Two competing modal-a11y systems now ship simultaneously. ModalPortal.tsx already exposes useRegisterModal() with LIFO stack + only-top-modal-receives-Esc + scroll lock on .lc-app. The new useModalDismiss hook duplicates the same concerns without integrating. When both are used (e.g. UploadPortal uses useRegisterModal @97 while Drawer uses useModalDismiss @75), each system independently applies a body scroll lock AND both fire on Esc.
findings.evidence: ModalPortal.tsx:78-89 registers a window keydown listener that dispatches to `stackRef.current[stackRef.current.length - 1]` (LIFO top). ModalPortal.tsx:61-75 sets `.lc-app` `overflow: hidden` while stackCount>0. Now useModalDismiss adds a SECOND window keydown listener that fires unconditionally when its own modal is open, AND a SECOND scroll lock on `document.body`. useRegisterModal callers: UploadPortal.tsx:97, ThumbnailPromptPreview.tsx:48. useModalDismiss callers: PublishModal, SubmitToWhopModal (publish), WatermarkTrialConfirmModal, EngineEditorOverlay, Drawer. If a UploadPortal-hosted route also renders a Drawer or PublishModal, both systems' Esc handlers fire (see P1-003). Double scroll lock is idempotent but the cleanup order is fragile.
findings.suggested_fix: Consolidate to one system. Preferred: extend useRegisterModal to also accept containerRef for focus trap (parity with useModalDismiss), then migrate all useModalDismiss callers to it. Alternative: retire useRegisterModal + ModalPortal's stack logic, migrate UploadPortal/ThumbnailPromptPreview to useModalDismiss, and add stack semantics to useModalDismiss (module-level LIFO ref). One system, one Esc listener, one scroll-lock owner.

findings.summary: Body scroll lock stacking breaks under non-LIFO close order. When Modal A opens then Modal B opens on top, then A closes before B, the body is unlocked while B is still visible.
findings.evidence: Line 76 · `const prev = document.body.style.overflow;` captures overflow at open-time via closure. A opens: prev_A='' set. B opens: prev_B='hidden' (A's write). If A closes first (unusual but possible if A's parent unmounts while B is a sibling), A's cleanup runs `document.body.style.overflow = ''` — body scrolls while B is still rendered. In normal LIFO close order (B closes first), works correctly. Edge case, not P1 because in practice modals close in stack order.
findings.reproduce: Manual: mount two useModalDismiss consumers, unmount the outer first while keeping the inner mounted, inspect document.body.style.overflow. Or read the closure semantics of lines 76-80.
findings.suggested_fix: Use a module-level counter or refcount: increment on open, decrement on cleanup, only restore body.overflow when count reaches 0. This is the same problem P1-005's consolidation would solve — ModalPortal already uses a proper stackCount pattern.

implementer_verification_answers.question: Does the LIFO stack correctly dequeue on modal unmount (not just open→false)? Check ModalPortal.tsx:139-142 cleanup.
implementer_verification_answers.evidence: ModalPortal.tsx:139 · useEffect(() => { if (!ctx || !opts.open) return; return ctx.register({ id: opts.id, onEscape: opts.onEscape }); }, [ctx, opts.id, opts.open, opts.onEscape]). React guarantees the returned cleanup runs on: (a) any dep change (opts.open flipping to false, id change, escape handler change), and (b) component unmount. In case (a), the effect body's early-return `if (!ctx || !opts.open) return;` means when open→false, the effect body returns undefined (no new registration) AND React first runs the previous return-value (the register's cleanup) before executing this branch. In case (b), unmount runs the last cleanup unconditionally. Both flows call ctx.register's returned cleanup at line 94-97 which filters the entry out by id and updates stackCount → triggers the scroll-lock useEffect at line 61-75. No orphan stack entries under any exit path.
